checks.value: Item 9C.Disclosure Regarding Foreign Jurisdictions that Prevent Inspections.

triage.note: Found by the T3-T5 cold review (G1 ledger row). segment.ADDED keys Item 9C to date(2022, 1, 1) and compares it against the filing's FISCAL PERIOD END. The SEC rule it encodes applies to annual reports FILED on or after 2022-01-01, which is a different date: every December-fiscal-year registrant that filed in Feb-Mar 2022 carries Item 9C with a period_end of 2021-12-31. Those filings are the largest single cohort on EDGAR for that season, and for all of them expected_items drops 9C, so segment.py never even makes the heading a CANDIDATE -- which is why no validator can catch it: 9C cannot appear in the rejected list, cannot appear in the TOC manifest, and therefore cannot raise toc_manifest_mismatch. Its text is silently annexed to Item 9B and the run can still report success. Keying to filing date is not implementable from the document alone -- only 2 of the 15 committed fixtures carry an SGML header with FILED AS OF DATE, and a modern primary .htm never does -- so the fix is to move the threshold back to the earliest period_end that can be filed under the new rule and let the existing auto-'omitted' path (segment.py, code in ('16','9C')) absorb filers that legitimately have no 9C heading. That auto-omit is itself an undocumented decision the same review flagged; it gets recorded in the ADR that moves this constant. NOTE the eval set actively encoded the wrong answer: sandston-2021-shallow pins the no-9C 21-item set as ground truth for a filing filed 2022-03-25. That case is correct about ITS fixture (grep confirms zero 9C occurrences in it -- the filer omitted the item) but for the wrong reason, and once the threshold moves it must assert 9C as 'omitted' rather than leaving it out of the expected set.

provenance:
SELF-CREATED adversarial fixture: a copy of evals/fixtures/sandston-2021/filing.htm (Sandston Corporation FY2021 10-K, EDGAR accession 0001410578-22-000504, filed 2022-03-25 -- see that fixture's README row for original public-source provenance), mutated 2026-08-16 by one documented, reproducible transformation. THE MUTATION: a 566-byte Item 9C block was INSERTED immediately after the 'None.

' that closes the Item 9B body paragraph, located from the body anchor 'Item9BOtherInformation_604096">' searched from raw offset 300000 so the table-of-contents copy of the same anchor (raw offset ~62913) cannot be hit by mistake. The inserted markup is a byte-for-byte copy of the filer's OWN Item 9B heading markup with only the code, the title and the body text changed -- same font-family/font-size/font-weight declarations, same 72pt inline-block span, same ' ' between 'Item' and the code -- so it is typographically indistinguishable from a real heading in this document and exercises no new normalization path. Content inserted: heading 'Item 9C. Disclosure Regarding Foreign Jurisdictions that Prevent Inspections.' and body 'Not applicable.'. Nothing is deleted, reordered, or otherwise altered; every byte outside the insertion point is identical to the source fixture. This mirrors the real filing shape exactly: a December-FY2021 registrant filing in March 2022 must address Item 9C, and 'Not applicable.' is the near-universal answer for a domestic filer. MEASURED EFFECT (run 2026-08-16 against the T5 pipeline, before any fix): no '9C' entry in items at all; Item 9B extracted at 166 chars against 71 in the unmutated source, i.e. it grew by exactly the inserted section, and its span text reads 'Item 9B.Other Information. None. Item 9C.Disclosure Regarding Foreign Jurisdictions that Prevent Inspections. Not applicable. ...' -- the annexation is directly visible in the output. doc_status 'success_with_warning', with the single warning 'unattributed_content' inherited unchanged from the source fixture and nothing at all attributable to the missing item. WHY THESE CHECKS: item_present(9C, extracted) is the direct assertion and fails today because the code is absent from the envelope entirely. Anchor counts verified by direct substring count on the mutated fixture's normalized text: 'Item 9C.Disclosure Regarding Foreign Jurisdictions that Prevent Inspections.' occurs exactly 1x -- there is no TOC row for it, since the mutation deliberately does not touch the table of contents, which also means this case does NOT depend on the TOC-manifest validator to notice anything. 'Not applicable.' occurs 2x (Item 7A's smaller-reporting-company response and the inserted 9C body), so it is used only as a text_contains scoped to item 9C, where a span containing it can only be the right one. max_chars(9B, 120) sits above 9B's true 71 chars and below the annexed 166, pinning the boundary numerically; the text_not_contains row pins the same bleed textually, and both are kept because text_not_contains is vacuous if 9B is ever not extracted. expected_set_complete and only_items carry the 22-item set -- the FY2021 21-item set of sandston-2021-shallow plus 9C. Per ADR-005 rule 1, a heading present with a trivial body ('Not applicable.') is 'extracted', not 'omitted'; that is why the status asserted here is extracted. NOT tagged 'invariant': the failure is confined to one item and its immediate neighbour rather than corrupting the whole document, so it belongs in the fast suite but does not need to be non-negotiable.
